summary.title: Embeddings: What they are and why they matter
summary.one_liner: Embeddings turn content into fixed-length arrays of numbers whose positions capture semantic meaning, enabling related-content lookup, vibes-based semantic search, clustering, classification and RAG.
takeaways: An embedding is a fixed-length array of floats representing content, where nearby locations in the space indicate related meaning.
Cosine similarity between embedding vectors can power related-content features and semantic (vibes-based) search that goes beyond exact keyword matches.
Word2Vec shows embeddings capturing relationships, such as vector arithmetic for germany + paris - france yielding berlin.
CLIP embeds text and images into the same vector space, enabling text-to-image and image-to-text search.
Embeddings can be clustered, reduced to 2D with PCA for visualization, used for classification via average locations, and used for retrieval-augmented question answering.
summary.summary: Simon Willison's article, adapted from a PyBay 2023 talk, explains embeddings as a trick for converting content into arrays of floating point numbers whose positions reflect semantic meaning. He walks through concrete examples: a related-articles feature for his TIL blog using OpenAI's text-embedding-ada-002 and SQLite, the Word2Vec demo with word arithmetic, and his LLM CLI tool running the open all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model for semantic search over README files. Further sections cover code search with Symbex, CLIP-based image search (including the Faucet Finder project), clustering via llm-cluster, 2D visualization with PCA, classification with average locations, and retrieval-augmented generation (the page is truncated before the RAG section ends).
